entries.title: Replication Fork Assembly on a Floating DNA Ladder
entries.description: A long double-helix tube slowly unwinds into two strands while colored spheres (helicase, primase, DNA polymerase) attach, detach, and slide along the strands, leaving growing chains of small beads (new nucleotides) that glow briefly as they snap into place.

entries.title: Helicase Motor Unzipping a Giant DNA Zipper
entries.description: A large torus-shaped “helicase” gear rotates and crawls along a vertical helical zipper, splitting the two strands apart into a widening Y-shaped fork while semi-transparent hydrogen-bond “springs” between bases stretch, snap, and vanish in bursts of particles.

entries.title: Leading vs Lagging Strand with Okazaki Fragments
entries.description: Two parallel template strands stretch across the scene as one side shows a smooth, continuous chain of beads forming (leading strand) and the other side shows short Okazaki fragments appearing, sliding together, and fusing with glowing pulses where ligase “bridges” connect them.
entries.seed: Leading vs Lagging Strand with Okazaki Fragments: Two parallel template strands stretch across the scene as one side shows a smooth, continuous chain of beads forming (leading strand) and the other side shows short Okazaki fragments appearing, sliding together, and fusing with glowing pulses where ligase “bridges” connect them.

entries.title: Replication Bubble Expanding in a Circular Chromosome
entries.description: A circular DNA ring lies flat while multiple replication bubbles appear as transparent ovals that expand; from each bubble, two forks move in opposite directions as colored beads representing nucleotides zip in from the surrounding fluid and attach to the exposed single strands.

entries.title: Base-Pair Matching and Proofreading Mini-Game
entries.description: A straightened single DNA strand moves slowly past the viewer while loose nucleotides of different colors float around and snap onto the strand; a polymerase “scanner” sphere glides behind, ejecting mismatched beads with small red flashes and leaving corrected beads that briefly glow green.

entries.title: Semi-Conservative Replication Color Transition
entries.description: An original helix made of red and white strands separates; each old strand (red) gains a new blue partner strand, so that two daughter helices form with half-red, half-blue composition, with a simple counter label updating the number of old vs new strands.

entries.title: Replication Factory with Multiple Forks in a Nucleus
entries.description: Inside a semi-transparent spherical nucleus, many DNA loops radiate from a central “replication factory” hub where several replication forks spin like a carousel, each fork pulling DNA through itself and leaving duplicated, differently colored segments that coil neatly behind.

entries.title: Topoisomerase Relieving DNA Supercoils
entries.description: A long helical cable twists and supercoils as helicase advances; a topoisomerase clamp periodically attaches to overwound regions, briefly cuts and rotates segments (seen as a small rotation and color pulse), then reseals them, visibly reducing the tension and untwisting the helix.

entries.title: Chromatin Unpacking and Replication
entries.description: DNA wrapped around colored histone spheres (nucleosomes) gradually unwraps, with the wraps rotating off like ribbons; exposed DNA segments are replicated by moving polymerase complexes, after which new nucleosomes (lighter colored) slide in and re-wrap the freshly copied DNA.

entries.title: Bidirectional Replication from Multiple Origins
entries.description: A long, slightly curved DNA fiber spans the scene with several “origin” markers that light up in sequence; from each origin, two forks emerge and move away in opposite directions, their progress shown by color-shifting the replicated regions and leaving faint trails indicating fork paths.

entries.title: Replication Under Resource Limitation Meter
entries.description: Nucleotide “fuel” beads in a side reservoir flow toward polymerases along thin tubes; as the reservoir level meter drops, polymerases slow and occasionally stall with blinking warning colors, then resume when more beads spill in, visually coupling replication speed to resource availability.

entries.title: DNA Damage and Repair During Replication
entries.description: Random segments of the template strand show as broken or mismatched (jagged or off-color) while polymerases approach; when they encounter damage, they stop and a repair complex attaches, excises a glowing red segment, replaces it with normal beads, then releases the polymerase to continue.

entries.title: Circular Plasmid Replication with Theta Structure
entries.description: A small circular plasmid hovers mid-air; as replication starts, a “theta” bubble forms with one replicated arm thicker and differently colored, and you can watch the replication fork move around the circle until the two rings separate and drift apart with a soft bounce.

entries.title: Mechanical City Metaphor for DNA Replication
entries.description: A factory-like city uses a central “blueprint spiral” (DNA helix) being uncoiled by crane arms while assembly robots (polymerases) run along conveyor belts (strands), picking colored blocks (nucleotides) from silos and snapping them into new parallel blueprint lanes with sparks when they mismatch.

entries.title: Replication vs Transcription Traffic on DNA
entries.description: A straight DNA track hosts both replication forks and smaller transcription complexes; replication forks move faster and are shown pushing or pausing transcription complexes when they collide, with short “traffic jam” clusters forming and then resolving as one complex detaches or moves aside.

entries.description: A thick DNA cable is sliced in the middle to reveal a cross-section bubble: two diverging forks are seen in 3D as colored channels where single strands are separated and coated by small protective proteins, while new strands grow inward and outward in a clear, labeled Y-shaped structure.

entries.description: A doughnut-shaped clamp sits around the DNA strand and slides smoothly as a polymerase sphere pushes it; when Okazaki fragments end, the clamp pops off with a quick spin, diffuses briefly, and is then reloaded ahead on the strand by a loader complex, leaving faint trails of its path.
